writingModel:
The Most Amazing Place I Have Ever Visited
By Kamila Seitkali

I have visited many beautiful places in Kazakhstan, but without a doubt, the most spectacular natural place I have ever seen is the Charyn Canyon in the Almaty region. I visited it last summer with my family, and the experience was absolutely unforgettable. I had seen photographs before, but nothing could have prepared me for the real thing.

Charyn Canyon is often called "the little Grand Canyon". It is approximately 200 kilometres east of Almaty, and the drive there takes about three hours. The canyon is 80 kilometres long and up to 300 metres deep in places. When you first see it, the reaction is immediate and physical — your breath catches, your heart beats faster, and you cannot speak. The colour of the rock is the most extraordinary thing: deep red and orange, turning to dark purple as the sun moves across the sky.

The landscape was absolutely breathtaking. The silence was completely deafening — no traffic, no city noise, just the sound of the wind and the occasional cry of a bird of prey circling overhead. The air was crisp and clean in a way that is totally different from city air. The valley below the main viewing platform is called the Valley of Castles, because the rock formations look like ancient towers and fortresses. I have never seen anything quite so impressive in my entire life.

The wildlife at Charyn is also remarkable. We spotted a golden eagle soaring above the canyon — enormous against the blue sky. In the canyon walls, we saw dozens of swallows darting in and out of their nests. The canyon is also home to the Sogdian ash tree — a relict species that has survived from the Ice Age and grows nowhere else in Kazakhstan. Seeing a living tree that has existed for millions of years was one of the most humbling experiences I have ever had.

I would absolutely recommend visiting Charyn Canyon to every WKU student. It is one of the most beautiful and most accessible natural wonders in our country. Go early in the morning when the light is best and the tourist crowds are smallest. Bring plenty of water — the canyon is absolutely scorching in summer — and wear comfortable shoes because the path down is steep and rocky. Most importantly, leave your phone in your bag for at least thirty minutes and simply stand there. Some experiences are too wonderful to filter through a screen.
